sections.h2: What does New Rochelle look like on the map?
sections.html:
New Rochelle is a Westchester County city on Long Island Sound, about 17 miles from Midtown Manhattan and two miles north of the Bronx line at Pelham Bay Park. The shape is a long triangle: roughly 10 miles from top to bottom and only 1.5 miles wide at the broadest point, with 10.29 square miles of land and 2.86 of water.

Pelham, Pelham Manor, Eastchester, Scarsdale, Mamaroneck and Larchmont all touch its borders. Inside the city, two houses a few blocks apart can feel like different towns: one near the downtown train hub, another on a leafy single-family street, a third on the water at Davenport Neck.

The 2020 census counted 79,726 residents, and the Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 85,864, up 7.7 percent from the 2020 estimates base.

sections.h2: How did New Rochelle start, and how does that show in the houses?
sections.html:
About 33 Huguenot families, many of them artisans from La Rochelle in France, founded the settlement in 1688 on land Thomas Pell had acquired from the Siwanoy in 1654. A village formed in 1857, and a charter signed in 1899 merged village and town into a single city.

Developers then carved farms and estates into planned districts. Rochelle Park, among the first planned communities in the country, helped win the nickname "City of Homes." Today the older streets lean Queen Anne, Tudor Revival and Colonial Revival, while the southwest corner has brownstones, townhomes and red-brick apartment buildings.

A house from that first building boom may carry decades of alterations. Old wiring, original windows or an enclosed porch built without a permit are the kind of items a buyer's inspector reports.

sections.h2: How many homes are there, and who lives in them?
sections.html:
More than 11,500 single-family houses stand in the city, alongside a downtown of condominiums, high rises and affordable housing complexes. The Census Bureau counts 31,684 households for 2020 to 2024, and owners occupy only 53.7 percent of housing units, so close to half of residents rent.

If you own a two-family or have a tenant in place, that renter share is your market. The survey's median gross rent is $1,917, and owners put the typical value of their homes at $702,500.

  • Median household income: $109,167 in 2024 dollars
  • Typical one-way commute: 32.5 minutes
  • Adults 25 and older with a four-year degree: 51.6 percent
  • Residents born outside the United States: 29.5 percent

The city names dozens of neighborhoods, among them Wykagyl, Beechmont, Rochelle Heights, Residence Park, Paine Heights, Bonnie Crest and Glenwood Lake. Premium Point and Pinebrook Hollow are gated.

sections.h2: How do the train, highways and schools affect a New Rochelle listing?
sections.html:
Access to Manhattan is the main selling point. Metro-North's New Haven Line and Amtrak's Northeast Regional both use the downtown station, Interstate 95 has four exits within the city, and the Boston Post Road serves as Main Street downtown. The Hutchinson River Parkway, closed to trucks, clogs both ways at rush hour.

The City School District of New Rochelle operates New Rochelle High School, two middle schools, six elementary schools and an early childhood center. Iona University, Mercy University's New Rochelle campus (formerly the College of New Rochelle) and Monroe College add a student population.

Westchester County Airport is nearby, and JFK and LaGuardia are reachable by road.

sections.h2: What does the New Rochelle economy look like?
sections.html:
The downtown was once industrial, with film studios, a diner manufacturer, a burner company and a soft-drink bottler among its past employers. Manufacturing and warehousing have faded since the 1990s, and land near both Interstate 95 exits has turned into big-box retail.

The mall site became New Roc City, a $190 million entertainment complex, and in 2014 the planning board approved $149 million of further downtown projects. The city has since granted tax breaks worth tens of millions of dollars to support redevelopment. Sidney Frank Importing, East River Savings Bank and Somnia Anesthesia Services are among the companies headquartered here.

sections.h2: Which tax bills does a New Rochelle owner pay, and when?
sections.html:
Expect four bills a year, so a mid-cycle closing has to apportion each of them. City taxes are due by January 31 for the calendar year, county taxes by June 30, and the school and library tax is split into a September 30 half and a March 31 half. Anything paid after the last day of the collection month picks up interest and penalties.

DateStep in the New Rochelle assessment and billing calendar
December 1Taxable status date, and last day to file exemptions
January 31City bill due
February 1Tentative assessment roll posted
Third Tuesday in FebruaryGrievance Day for assessment complaints
March 31School and library bill, second half
April 1Final roll
June 30Westchester County bill due
September 30School and library bill, first half

Source: City of New Rochelle assessments and property tax schedule pages.

The assessor's office says there has been no citywide revaluation since 1956. Instead, each addition or renovation is judged as of December 1 and shows up on the following February roll. A buyer of a freshly renovated house may therefore face a higher bill than you paid.

sections.h2: Where does the deed go, and who changes the owner of record?
sections.html:
The Westchester County Clerk, not City Hall, handles the recording. The assessor's FAQ states that ownership records cannot be edited at the city level and sends owners to an attorney and the county.

The clerk will take a deed only with paperwork generated in its PREP online system:

  • A recording and endorsement cover page
  • Form TP-584, the state transfer tax return
  • Form RP-5217, the Real Property Transfer Report
  • A payment cover page covering fees and tax

The state levies $2 per $500 of consideration, rounded up to the next $500. In the clerk's own illustration, a price of $404,501 is treated as $405,000 and costs $1,620. By default that tax is the seller's. A 1 percent mansion tax applies to residences at $1 million and up and falls on the buyer. Your closing attorney can confirm totals for your deed.

sections.h2: Which permits can complicate a New Rochelle sale?
sections.html:
Unclosed permits and gaps in occupancy paperwork are the usual trouble spots. The city explains that building permits are a New York State requirement and takes applications through an online system. No permit is needed to paint outside the Historical district, to resurface a one or two-family driveway without widening it, or to lay siding over existing wall surfaces without replacing the sheathing.

If an earlier owner finished a deck, attic or basement and never closed the permit, the buyer's attorney will want the paper trail. A cash buyer taking the house as-is can accept those gaps, though the offer will reflect them. Call the city's building permit office about your address before accepting any bid.

If you receive the STAR credit, close that registration with the state once the sale is done. The buyer registers through the Homeowner Benefit Portal when the house becomes their primary residence.

faqs.q: Which four bills does a New Rochelle homeowner receive?
faqs.a: The city, Westchester County, and the school and library taxes in two halves. City taxes are due January 31, county taxes June 30, and the school halves September 30 and March 31.

faqs.q: Does an open building permit block a New Rochelle sale?
faqs.a: It does not stop a sale, but the buyer inherits the problem, so expect a lower bid or a request to close it first. Ask the city's building permit office which applications are open on your address.

faqs.q: What date is Grievance Day in New Rochelle?
faqs.a: The third Tuesday in February, following the February 1 tentative roll. Exemption forms are due December 1, and the final roll is set April 1.

faqs.q: Which office records a New Rochelle deed?
faqs.a: The Westchester County Clerk, using cover pages and forms created in the PREP system. City staff cannot change ownership records, so the deed and the TP-584 go to the county.

faqs.q: Has New Rochelle revalued every home recently?
faqs.a: No. The assessor's office says there has been no citywide reassessment since 1956. Improvements are reviewed one at a time as of December 1.
